summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Mango and Coconut are Drupes (stony hard endocarp). Mango has edible fleshy mesocarp; Coconut has fibrous mesocarp (coir source) and edible liquid/cellular endosperm.

conceptBreakdown.content: A true fruit (**Eucarp**) is a mature, ripened ovary developed after fertilization. If non-ovarian floral parts (e.g., thalamus, pedicel, calyx) participate in fruit formation, it is termed a **False Fruit / Pseudocarp** (*Apple*, *Strawberry*, *Pear*). A fruit developed without fertilization is **Parthenocarpic** (*Banana*).

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 Drupe vs. Berry Anatomy
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Drupe vs. Berry Anatomy
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Drupe (Stone Fruit)**: Developed from monocarpellary or multicarpellary syncarpous, superior ovaries. Characterized by a three-layered pericarp featuring a **stony hard Endocarp**:
  - **Mango (*Mangifera indica*)**: Thin Epicarp (skin), fleshy edible Mesocarp, and hard stony Endocarp enclosing the seed.
  - **Coconut (*Cocos nucifera*)**: Thin smooth Epicarp, fibrous Mesocarp (commercial source of coir), and stony Endocarp enclosing liquid endosperm ("coconut water") and cellular endosperm.
• **Berry**: Fleshy, pulpy multi-seeded fruit lacking a stony endocarp; epicarp is thin, and mesocarp and endocarp fuse to form succulent edible pulp (*Tomato*, *Brinjal*, *Guava*, *Grape*).
